boards.school_name: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free, documented cultural and campus-adjacent places for an under-21 Syracuse outing.

cards.title: Syracuse University Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Shaffer Art Building, Syracuse University
cards.notes: Pick an exhibition, meet at the museum entrance, and give each person time to choose one work to discuss afterward.
cards.short_summary: A free public art museum on the neighboring Syracuse University campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Syracuse University Art Museum states that it is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; check the museum’s current exhibition and visitor information before going.

cards.entity_name: Public Art @ SU Self-Guided Audio Tour
cards.title: Public Art @ SU Audio Tour
cards.subtitle: Syracuse University campus
cards.notes: Download the free guide before leaving, then follow the self-guided route together and pause at works that invite a closer look.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided route connecting public artworks across the neighboring campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University Art Museum offers a self-guided Public Art @ SU audio tour through Bloomberg Connects, available through a free download.
cards.source_title: Your Digital Guide to the Syracuse University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: The official guide states that the app download is free; use open campus pedestrian routes and follow campus rules.

cards.title: Light Work Galleries
cards.subtitle: Robert B. Menschel Media Center, 316 Waverly Avenue
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition first, then meet in the gallery and compare one photograph or moving-image work that caught each person’s eye.
cards.short_summary: Free public galleries focused on photography and related media.
cards.evidence_claim: Light Work states that its galleries are free and open to the public at the Robert B. Menschel Media Center.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; the gallery asks visitors to call to verify it is open.

cards.title: Warehouse Gallery
cards.subtitle: Nancy Cantor Warehouse, 350 West Fayette Street
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided gallery stop during posted hours, then use the exhibition as a prompt for a low-key conversation or sketch session.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Syracuse University gallery with free public entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University’s Warehouse Gallery states that the gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during listed gallery hours; self-guided groups over six should contact the gallery in advance.

cards.title: Erie Canal Museum
cards.subtitle: 318 Erie Boulevard East, downtown Syracuse
cards.notes: Walk through the permanent exhibits together and use the weighlock building as a starting point for talking about Syracuse’s canal history.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission history museum in the former 1850 Syracuse Weighlock Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Erie Canal Museum states that it is open seven days a week with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Official museum information says admission is free; check current visitor hours before arrival.

cards.title: Bird Library
cards.subtitle: 222 Waverly Avenue, Syracuse University
cards.notes: Meet in an open study area, bring your own materials, and use the public-access window for a focused group work or reading session.
cards.short_summary: A large nearby academic library with public daytime access and open study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University Libraries states that Bird Library is open to the public daily until 7 p.m. on regular business days and lists open study areas.
cards.access_notes: Public entry is available until 7 p.m. on regular business days; no admission or purchase is required for the listed open study areas.

cards.title: Moon Library Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: SUNY ESF campus
cards.notes: Use a group study space or the lobby for a calm catch-up between classes; keep the visit quiet and follow library community guidelines.
cards.short_summary: ESF’s library offers student spaces for collaborative work and quiet breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: Moon Library’s policy describes spaces for meeting, discussion, collaborative work, relaxation, and quiet time; ESF affiliates can use designated after-hours study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Library study use requires no admission or purchase. After-hours access is limited to ESF students, faculty, and staff with activated ESF ID.

cards.title: Gateway Center Green Roof
cards.subtitle: SUNY ESF campus
cards.notes: Meet on the seated green roof, identify a few native plant forms, and keep the visit to the designated accessible areas.
cards.short_summary: An ESF demonstration landscape with seating and native-plant research.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF states that Gateway Center’s green roof has seating areas, is accessible to visitors, and serves research and demonstration purposes.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to visitors according to ESF; use designated areas and current building-access procedures. No admission or purchase is required to visit the roof.

cards.title: Roosevelt Wild Life Collection Exhibit
cards.subtitle: Gateway Center concourse, SUNY ESF
cards.notes: Look over the displayed specimens in the concourse, choose one to investigate later, and leave collections and display cases untouched.
cards.short_summary: A publicly viewable selection of ESF natural-history specimens.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF states that many Roosevelt Wild Life Collection specimens are displayed in Gateway Center’s main-floor concourse and are easily viewable by all.
cards.access_notes: ESF says the specimens are easily viewable by all in the concourse; comply with current building-access rules. Viewing requires no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Thornden Park
cards.subtitle: 201 Ostrom Avenue, Syracuse
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk on the paved trails, settle at a picnic table, or visit the rose-garden area while respecting posted park rules.
cards.short_summary: A 76-acre city park near campus with trails, green space, and a rose garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Syracuse identifies Thornden Park as a 76-acre public park with paved walking trails, picnic tables, and the E.M. Mills Rose Garden; city parks are open daily dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: City parks are open daily from dawn to dusk; walking and informal use require no admission or purchase. Follow posted park rules.
